findings.category: Cluster identity or node-local data convergence fails across reboots or rejoin. Membership recovery is distinguished from complete data resynchronization.
findings.title: RabbitMQ reboot changed its hostname and broke the cluster identity
findings.classification_basis: DHCP reset node1's hostname after reboot, so RabbitMQ started under a new, unclustered node identity. Repair began but the trace ended before rejoin was confirmed; the final snapshot had no node1 AMQP/TLS or management listener. Peers remained healthy. The cluster's unattended identity persistence failed.

072. RabbitMQ reboot changed its hostname and broke the cluster identity
Batch: 5469 | Execution: 2026-09-04__19-04-22 | Severity: Medium
Task: rabbitmq-tls-bash-alpine-5469
Problem: DHCP reset node1's hostname after reboot, so RabbitMQ started under a new, unclustered node identity. Repair began but the trace ended before rejoin was confirmed; the final snapshot had no node1 AMQP/TLS or management listener. Peers remained healthy. The cluster's unattended identity persistence failed.
Why a production administrator should care: A service that works only after human intervention may fail during unattended restarts. The final persistence repair needs its own functional test.

findings.title: Object-store rejoin required manual healing to restore a local shard
findings.classification_basis: A returning node rejoined automatically, but it lacked the object's local shard until an explicit mc admin heal changed the status from Yellow to Green. The trace supports automatic membership recovery, not automatic local resynchronization. No unrecoverable object loss is established.
